points.title: Defining relative clauses
points.function: who for people; which/that for things
examples: A friend is someone who supports you.
This is the message that I sent.

points.title: Too and enough
examples: She was calm enough to listen.

tip.title: Accuracy Tip

sections.title: Listening: Relationships & Communication
sections.description: Listen once for gist and again for detail.

audio.transcript: My closest friend is someone who lives in another city. We enjoy sending voice messages because they feel more personal than short texts. Last week, we had an argument about a plan that changed at the last minute. I was too annoyed to listen properly. Later, I realised she had a good reason, so I apologised. We are close enough to discuss problems honestly, and that helps us keep in touch.

gistQuestions.prompt: What is the talk mainly about?
options: Repairing a friendship after an argument
gistQuestions.explanation: The complete recording supports this main idea.

detailQuestions.prompt: Why do the friends like voice messages?
detailQuestions.explanation: This detail is stated in the recording. Read the complete context before rejecting the other options.

tip.title: Listening Strategy
tip.text: Use the first listen for context and the second listen to confirm exact details.

sections.title: Speaking: Relationships & Communication
sections.description: Prepare briefly, record your response and review it.
questions: Describe a person you communicate with often.
How do you keep in touch?
sections.sampleAnswer: My best friend is someone who listens carefully. We enjoy talking after work and keep in touch by message. We are honest enough to solve small disagreements quickly.
prompts: Answer every part of the prompt.

tip.title: Speaking Tip
tip.text: Organise your answer into a clear beginning, two details and a short ending.
